_work.title: Barchusen — Elementa Chemiae (Utrecht, 1718): Alchemical Emblem Plates
_work.blurb: The 78 copper-engraved emblem plates from Johann Conrad Barchusen's encyclopedic Elementa Chemiae (Utrecht, 1718), derived directly from a manuscript of The Crowning of Nature (Coronatio Naturae). These engravings represent the first and only major printed edition of the Crowning of Nature emblem sequence, depicting the stages of the philosopher's stone through sequential allegorical images: toad, dragon, crowned king and queen, alchemical vessel, putrefaction, conjunction, multiplication, and projection.

entries.title: Barchusen Elementa Chemiae — Title Page (1718)
entries.summary: Title page of Johann Conrad Barchusen's Elementa Chemiae (Utrecht, 1718). The full Latin title translates as 'Elements of Chemistry: to which is appended the preparation of the philosopher's stone represented by images.' Held at the Science History Institute, Philadelphia. Barchusen (1666–1723) was professor of chemistry at Utrecht University 1703–23, one of the last systematic defenders of iatrochemical alchemy in the age of Boyle and Newton.

entries.title: Barchusen's Laboratory at the University of Utrecht — Page 61
entries.summary: Engraving from page 61 of the Elementa Chemiae depicting Barchusen's laboratory at the University of Utrecht. Shows a spacious chemistry laboratory with furnaces, fume hoods, and apparatus. A scientist is shown at a table with instruments and materials. Contextualized the alchemical emblem plates that follow in the treatise.

entries.title: Barchusen in His Laboratory at Sonnenborgh, Utrecht
entries.summary: Engraving depicting Johann Conrad Barchusen (1666–1723) in his laboratory on the Sonnenborgh hill in Utrecht, from the Elementa Chemiae (1718). The Sonnenborgh observatory building housed Barchusen's experimental facilities. The image anchors the alchemical emblem sequence in a real, identifiable scientific workspace.

entries.title: Barchusen Elementa Chemiae — Tab. 3: Alchemical Emblems with Apparatus Key
entries.summary: Tabula 3 from Elementa Chemiae (1718). Juxtaposes Crowning of Nature allegorical imagery with diagrams of the chemical apparatus used in the depicted procedures — Barchusen's key method of demystifying alchemical symbolism through practical chemical documentation. Held at the Science History Institute, Philadelphia.

entries.title: Barchusen Elementa Chemiae — Tab. 4: Alchemical Emblems with Apparatus Key
entries.summary: Tabula 4 from Elementa Chemiae (1718). Pairs Crowning of Nature allegorical imagery with chemical apparatus descriptions, exemplifying Barchusen's late-alchemical project of rational interpretation. Held at the Science History Institute, Philadelphia.

entries.title: Barchusen Elementa Chemiae — Tab. 5: Alchemical Emblems with Apparatus Key
entries.summary: Tabula 5 from Elementa Chemiae (1718). Presents Crowning of Nature allegorical imagery alongside diagrams of chemical apparatus, representing Barchusen's systematic effort to demystify alchemical practice at the end of alchemy's academic prominence in Europe. Held at the Science History Institute, Philadelphia.

entries.title: Elementa Chemiae — Plate 503, Figs. 1–5: Crowning of Nature Emblems 1–5
entries.summary: Opening page of the Crowning of Nature emblem sequence in Barchusen's Elementa Chemiae, figures 1–5. Each circular allegorical emblem is paired with a depiction of the chemical apparatus used in the procedure it represents — the prima materia, initial preparation, and first dissolution stages of the Great Work. Held at the Science History Institute, Philadelphia.

entries.title: Elementa Chemiae — Plate 503, Figs. 6–9: Crowning of Nature Emblems 6–9
entries.summary: Emblems 6–9 of the Crowning of Nature sequence, from Barchusen's Elementa Chemiae. Each circular emblem is paired with chemical apparatus diagrams. Likely shows the dissolution, putrefaction (nigredo), and early albedo stages. Held at the Science History Institute, Philadelphia.

entries.title: Elementa Chemiae — Plate 504, Figs. 10–13: Crowning of Nature Emblems 10–13
entries.summary: Emblems 10–13 of the Crowning of Nature sequence, from Barchusen's Elementa Chemiae. Each allegorical circular image is juxtaposed with chemical apparatus diagrams. Likely shows albedo (whitening), the moon stages, and early coniunctio. Held at the Science History Institute, Philadelphia.

entries.title: Elementa Chemiae — Plate 505, Figs. 14–17: Crowning of Nature Emblems 14–17 (high-res)
entries.summary: High-resolution scan (3492 × 4614 px) of emblems 14–17 of the Crowning of Nature sequence, from Barchusen's Elementa Chemiae. This AQ26 archival scan is the finest-quality image in the Barchusen Commons set. Emblems 14–17 likely depict the rubedo (reddening), king and queen conjunction, and advanced stages. Held at the Science History Institute, Philadelphia.

entries.title: Elementa Chemiae — Plate 505, Figs. 18–21: Crowning of Nature Emblems 18–21
entries.summary: Emblems 18–21 of the Crowning of Nature sequence, from Barchusen's Elementa Chemiae. Emblems 22–37 are not represented in the Commons set (gap in coverage). Held at the Science History Institute, Philadelphia.

entries.title: Elementa Chemiae — Plate 509, Figs. 38–41: Crowning of Nature Emblems 38–41
entries.summary: Emblems 38–41 of the Crowning of Nature sequence, from Barchusen's Elementa Chemiae (note: emblems 22–37 and 42–45 are not in the Commons set). Mid-sequence emblems likely depict multiplication and fermentation stages. Held at the Science History Institute, Philadelphia.

entries.title: Elementa Chemiae — Plate 510, Figs. 46–49: Crowning of Nature Emblems 46–49
entries.summary: Emblems 46–49 of the Crowning of Nature sequence, from Barchusen's Elementa Chemiae. Late-middle stages of the Great Work sequence, likely depicting advanced projection or fixation stages. Held at the Science History Institute, Philadelphia.

entries.title: Elementa Chemiae — Plate 512, Figs. 50–53: Crowning of Nature Emblems 50–53
entries.summary: Emblems 50–53 of the Crowning of Nature sequence, from Barchusen's Elementa Chemiae. Later stages of the Great Work, approaching the completion of the Stone. Each circular emblem paired with chemical apparatus. Held at the Science History Institute, Philadelphia.

entries.title: Elementa Chemiae — Plate 512, Figs. 54–57: Crowning of Nature Emblems 54–57
entries.summary: Emblems 54–57 of the Crowning of Nature sequence, from Barchusen's Elementa Chemiae. Late stages of the Great Work. Each allegorical image paired with chemical apparatus to clarify the alchemical process. Held at the Science History Institute, Philadelphia.

entries.title: Elementa Chemiae — Plate 512, Figs. 58–61: Crowning of Nature Emblems 58–61
entries.summary: Emblems 58–61 of the Crowning of Nature sequence, from Barchusen's Elementa Chemiae. Near-final stages of the philosopher's stone preparation sequence. Combines symbolic imagery with laboratory apparatus documentation. Held at the Science History Institute, Philadelphia.

entries.title: Elementa Chemiae — Plate 512, Figs. 74–78: Crowning of Nature Emblems 74–78 (Final)
entries.summary: Final emblems 74–78 of the Crowning of Nature sequence in Barchusen's Elementa Chemiae (emblems 62–73 not in Commons set). These concluding plates represent the projection, multiplication, and completion stages — the crowning achievement of the philosopher's stone. Held at the Science History Institute, Philadelphia.
